tested_on.host: Hermes agent on an openclawlaunch Linux container: 16 vCPU, 62 GiB RAM; headless-Linux numbers; real-device behavior is NOT_RUN

A32.notes: Chromium-only platform ID (the share-target POST route, as A08). A real multipart POST through the service worker (the same handler Android's share sheet hits) starts OCR automatically, shows the one progress state (role=status), and lands on the result screen with the large Copy button fully above the fold at 390x844; clicking Copy puts exactly the result text on the real clipboard. The share POST body is never cached or logged (the A15 audit re-ran on this flow). Real installed-PWA sharing stays A27 NOT_RUN.

A33.notes: Both engines: every arrival channel lands on the result-first screen — the pick path is the engine-neutral channel (the share path is A32's, the host-message path is R2-2's). Copy is the first, primary action (1.2x+ the Share button in both dimensions) and fully above the fold at 390x844; Share and the file-save menu follow; the editable text comes after the actions; no drop zone, paste button, model card or model toggle sits on the reading/result path (the model opt-in is collapsed inside #advanced-cleanup — asserted on the real ready model in the a21 spec). Heading renamed 'Review' -> 'Your text' per the R2-1 mockups; the 17 existing heading assertions changed with it in the same PR (plan rule G2).

Labelling which extracted words came from INSIDE pictures is not implemented: OCR returns text, not image-region segmentation, and no segmentation model ships — the nested text is included in the single text flow, and the limit is disclosed in KNOWN_LIMITS.md rather than faked.
The share-target POST route (A32/A36) is Chromium-only (as A08): WebKit-on-Linux does not serve the service-worker share route; the WebKit coverage of the result-first screen is A33's pick path.
Real installed-PWA sharing (Android) and the real iOS share sheet stay NOT_RUN (A27, the plan's optional real-device pass; checklist in docs/KNOWN_LIMITS.md).
iPhone cannot receive shares in a plain web app — the supported route is the host mobile app (R2-2), documented honestly in docs/INTEGRATION.md.
